english.note: For ordinary physical departure or telling someone to go away, 走 is the all-purpose choice; in context it can also mean quitting a group or organization.
This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for leaving or departing from a place or situation.
Use 走 as the all-purpose casual verb when someone is leaving or going away.
Use this for going or hurrying away, especially fleeing from trouble rather than literally running on foot.
Use this colloquial verb when “shoot” means leave quickly.
Use this colloquial departure sense when “roll” means to leave or get going, as in 走啦.
Use this colloquially when “split” means to leave or go away.
